evidence: The survivor orders vertices by "descending degree for better pruning" and its code is explicitly solving the three-color assignment problem; the defeated traces likewise say "Try to color the graph with 3 colors".
affordance_in_statement: Each module must be assigned an environment identifier "e_i in {1, 2, 3}" and every constraint requires "|e_u - e_v| >= 1".
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving wording change that removes this affordance: the stated task is intrinsically graph 3-colorability. It can only be re-presented indirectly by explicitly warning that inputs may be adversarial, dense, and selected to force exhaustive search, with no promise of sparsity or easy branching.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the task as exact 3-coloring and uses degree-based branching/pruning.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The identifiers are restricted to three values and each constraint requires the two endpoint identifiers to differ.

common_affordance: The intrinsic reduction of the constraints to exact 3-coloring with three available colors

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Uses naive fixed-index backtracking over up to three colors, causing exponential search and TLE on hard instances.
Also applies ordinary 3-color backtracking without sufficiently strong variable ordering or pruning, so it times out on worst-case graphs.

recommended_edit: Add a mutable scenario guarantee that the test data includes adversarial dense graphs specifically chosen to defeat fixed-order and simple degree-order backtracking, while retaining the same input, output, bounds, and correctness task.
